0.headline: South-based A-One Steels India to open Rs 405-crore IPO on September 24
0.heading: South-based A-One Steels India to open Rs 405-crore IPO on September 24
0.intro: A-One Steels India IPO | The company aims to raise Rs 355 crore through the issuance of fresh shares, while promoters will sell shares worth Rs 55 crore through an offer for sale.
0.body:
South-based steel producer A-One Steels India has tapped the capital markets to raise Rs 405 crore through an initial public offering (IPO). The IPO will open for public subscription on September 24 and close on September 28.

The one-day anchor book will open for institutional investors on September 23. The company is expected to finalise the IPO share allotment by September 29, while its equity shares are likely to begin trading on the bourses from October 1.

The company aims to raise Rs 355 crore through the issuance of fresh shares, while promoters will sell shares worth Rs 55 crore through an offer for sale (OFS), according to the red herring prospectus filed with the Registrar of Companies on September 11.

The issue size has been reduced from the Rs 650 crore planned earlier in the draft offer document filed with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in December 2024. The capital markets regulator subsequently approved the IPO papers in May 2025.

The company will announce the price band details separately next week.

A-One Steels India manufactures long and flat steel products, as well as industrial products used in steel manufacturing. The company operates through six manufacturing units across Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, with a total capacity of 17,33,100 MTPA.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

The company intends to utilise Rs 250 crore from the net proceeds of the fresh issue to repay debt, against total standalone outstanding borrowings of Rs 864.4 crore as of July 15, 2026. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

A-One Steels India reported a profit of Rs 127.4 crore for the fiscal year ended March 2026, more than 16 times the Rs 7.7 crore profit recorded in the previous year. Revenue rose 17.1 percent to Rs 4,148.6 crore from Rs 3,541.8 crore during the same period.

PL Capital Markets and Khambatta Securities have been appointed as the merchant bankers for the A-One Steels India IPO.

1.headline: IPO action: NSE among 11 issues worth Rs 24,600 crore opening next week
1.heading: IPO action: NSE among 11 issues worth Rs 24,600 crore opening next week
1.intro: The total fundraising through the 11 initial public offerings is estimated at Rs 24,574.28 crore. Of this, five mainboard IPOs account for Rs 24,328.02 crore, while six issues in the SME segment are expected to raise Rs 246.26 crore.
1.body:
The bullish sentiment in the primary market has remained undampened by the weakness in the secondary market, with nearly Rs 24,600 crore worth of 11 IPOs set to open for public subscription in the holiday-shortened week beginning September 15.

However, the equity market fell more than 2 percent last week and has corrected nearly 6 percent from its August high, as bears tightened their grip amid expectations of prolonged Middle East tensions, elevated oil prices and rising US bond yields.

The total fundraising through the 11 initial public offerings (IPOs) is estimated at Rs 24,574.28 crore. Of this, five mainboard IPOs account for Rs 24,328.02 crore, while six issues in the SME segment are expected to raise Rs 246.26 crore.

The much-awaited National Stock Exchange of India's (NSE) Rs 22,561.6-crore maiden public issue will open for subscription on September 17, with a price band of Rs 1,700-1,785 per share, and close on September 21. The anchor book will open on September 16. Source-based reports indicate that Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) is expected to be the biggest investor in the anchor book, while Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, GIC, Fidelity, SBI Life and HDFC Life are also likely to participate.

The IPO is entirely an offer for sale (OFS) by 10 existing shareholders, including State Bank of India, Canara Pension Plan Investment Board, Aranda Investments, MS Strategic, New India Assurance Company and SBI Capital Markets. Therefore, the issue proceeds, excluding offer-related expenses, will be received by the selling shareholders, and the NSE will not receive any proceeds from the offer.

The primary objective of the IPO is to facilitate the NSE's listing on the BSE, along with carrying out the proposed offer for sale.

Automobile parts maker Hero Motors, promoted by O P Munjal Holdings, will be the next-largest mainboard IPO, with an issue size of Rs 1,000 crore. The IPO will open on September 16 and close on September 18, with a price band of Rs 79-84 per share. The public issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 600 crore and an OFS of Rs 400 crore by the promoters.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

SS Retail, a multi-brand retail chain selling mobile phones, accessories and other electronic products, and steel pipes and tubes maker Jindal Supreme (India) will also open their public issues on September 16. This will be followed by the IPO of textile products manufacturer Sonaselection India on September 17.

SS Retail aims to raise Rs 500 crore through its maiden public issue at the upper end of the price band of Rs 403-424 per share. The issue comprises a fresh issue of Rs 360 crore and an OFS of Rs 140 crore by existing shareholders.

Jindal Supreme (India) is looking to mobilise Rs 124.88 crore by issuing 1.34 crore equity shares at the upper end of the price band of Rs 88-93 per share. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of 1.07 crore equity shares and an OFS of 26.86 lakh shares by a promoter entity.

The 1.43-crore-share IPO of Sonaselection India will raise Rs 141.57 crore and comprises an entirely fresh issue. The price band has been fixed at Rs 94-99 per share.

SME
Vama Wovenfab, Quanto Agroworld and Shakti Polytarp will be the first SME issues to hit Dalal Street next week. All three IPOs will open on September 15 and close on September 17.

Vama Wovenfab, a manufacturer of PP and HDPE woven sack bags and fabric-based packaging products, is raising Rs 49.54 crore through its IPO at the upper end of the price band of Rs 324-341 per share.

Quanto Agroworld, which operates as a specialty ingredient manufacturer focused on lemongrass-based botanical formats and essential oils, intends to mobilise Rs 31.02 crore through its public issue at a fixed price of Rs 67 per share.

The 45.64-lakh-share IPO of Shakti Polytarp, a manufacturer of tarpaulins, will raise Rs 26.93 crore.

Kheria Autocomp and SpectraA Technology Solutions will open their maiden public issues on September 17 and close them on September 21. Meanwhile, the IPO of Axiom Gas Engineering will open on September 18 and close on September 22, with a price band of Rs 50-53 per share.

Kheria Autocomp, which manufactures plastic components primarily for the automotive sector, intends to raise Rs 46.44 crore at the upper end of the price band of Rs 96-101 per share.

The 36.03-lakh-share IPO of engineering and technology solutions provider SpectraA Technology Solutions will raise Rs 42.5 crore at the upper end of the price band of Rs 112-118 per share.

Axiom Gas Engineering, which provides auto LPG, CNG and LNG solutions to retail and industrial sectors, aims to mobilise Rs 49.81 crore through its initial share sale.

IPOs Closing Next Week
In the mainboard segment, Kerala-based real estate developer Veegaland Developers will close its maiden public issue on September 15, while the IPO of plastic products maker Manika Plastech will remain open until September 16.

In the SME segment, the public issues of Raksan Transformers, Maharaja &amp; Speedex India, Om Galaxy and Panchatv Bharat will close for subscription on September 15. The IPOs of Injecto Polymers and Century Business Media will remain open until September 16.

New Listings Next Week
The listing schedule is also expected to be busy next week, with 19 new companies set to begin trading on the bourses, including 11 from the mainboard segment.

Pranav Constructions will be the first mainboard company to list, on September 15, followed by Kanohar Electricals, Prasol Chemicals and Glass Wall Systems (India) on September 16.

The maximum number of listings is scheduled for September 17. Rentomojo, Asset Reconstruction Company India, Karamtara Engineering, LCC Projects, Manipal Payment &amp; Identity Solutions and Steamhouse India are scheduled to begin trading on the stock exchanges that day.

Veegaland Developers is expected to make its market debut on September 18.

In the SME segment, Apana Logistics will be the first to begin trading, on September 15, followed by Infrax Renewable, Amtech Esters and Vinod Texworld on September 17.

On the final trading day of the week, September 18, four companies — Maharaja &amp; Speedex India, Raksan Transformers, Panchatv Bharat, and Om Galaxy are likely to be available for trading on the SME platforms.

2.headline: SML Ltd weighing IPO within 2 to 3 years, eyes new chemical entity pipeline
2.heading: SML Ltd weighing IPO within 2 to 3 years, eyes new chemical entity pipeline
2.intro: The listing deliberations come as SML pushes deeper into three business lines beyond its traditional sulphur fertilizer base: crop nutrition, crop protection and biologicals
2.body:
Agri-inputs maker SML Ltd, formerly known as Sulphur India Limited, is evaluating a stock market listing within the next two to three years as it looks to fund the development of new chemical entities (NCEs), Managing Director Bimal Shah said.

"We have not completely decided — we are also evaluating it," Shah said in an interview to PTI, adding that the debt-free company expects greater clarity on the timeline within the next one to two years.

Mumbai-based SML Ltd said it is among a handful of Indian companies developing NCEs — proprietary new molecules rather than generic formulations — with one new molecule expected to reach the market soon and others in the pipeline.

"We are working on NCEs, new chemical entity in the last three years. We have a new molecule coming up very soon. … NCE is a very important focus for us. Of course, this requires a lot of investment," he said.

Bringing a single NCE to market can cost $70 million-$80 million, Shah said, and the company has so far self-financed the research.

These considerations may eventually lead the company toward listing, but no decision has been made yet; it's still evaluating, Shah said, adding that he expects to have a "clearer sense of direction this year or next", since further steps will depend on related groundwork being completed.

CASH PILE, ACQUISITION TARGETS

SML Ltd holds roughly Rs 450-470 crore in cash on a near debt-free balance sheet; funds, Shah said, could be deployed toward acquisitions, regulatory assets or strategic tie-ups, alongside the NCE program.

The company pointed to its earlier increase in ownership of Rotam India, an active ingredient manufacturing facility, as an example of the kind of backwards-integration deal it could pursue again.

"We've maintained a stable balance sheet over the years, and this accumulated fund is intended for the right opportunity — potentially an acquisition, strategic tie-up, or backward integration," he said.

The listing deliberations come as SML pushes deeper into three business lines beyond its traditional sulphur fertilizer base: crop nutrition, crop protection and biologicals.

Shah said crop nutrition, where the company is promoting balanced, nutrient-efficient formulations rather than single-nutrient products, is likely to be the fastest-growing of the three over the next three years, both in India and globally.

REVENUE OUTLOOK TRIMMED

SML has lowered its revenue target for the current fiscal year to about Rs 1,600 crore, from an earlier goal of Rs 1,800 crore, citing weaker monsoon rainfall, US tariffs and shipping disruptions tied to ongoing geopolitical conflict. That would still mark an increase from roughly Rs 1,200-1,300 crore a year earlier, aided by price increases of 15-20 per cent across its product range.

International business, spanning more than 80 countries, generated roughly Rs 600-700 crore last fiscal year; SML is targeting Rs 700-800 crore this year and Rs 1,000 crore within two years, though it flagged continued tariff and shipping-related uncertainty.

Roughly 70 per cent of SML's export revenue comes from crop-protection products, including insecticides and fungicides using microencapsulation and water-dispersible granule technologies, the executive said.

BRAND PUSH

SML Ltd separately unveiled cricket icon Sachin Tendulkar as its brand ambassador this year, betting his national profile can accelerate farmer adoption of its sulphur-based fertilizers. The company estimates only a small fraction of India's farmland currently receives adequate sulphur nutrition, despite government soil surveys showing widespread deficiency.

"We are trying to connect nutrition, sports and agriculture together," Shah said, adding that Tendulkar had sought out the partnership after noting he had never worked with an agriculture-focused company before.

The company recently launched seven new products across crop protection and crop nutrition. Shah said crop protection products converts to sales faster since it operates on an AI-to-AI (active ingredient) basis. "We expect at least an additional Rs 100 crore this year from these new products/technologies, with crop nutrition potentially contributing even more depending on market reach and consumption growth."

SUPPLY GAP

India's fertilizer industry has increasingly flagged sulphur deficiency as a hidden constraint on crop yields, with government soil-health surveys showing widespread shortfalls nationally.

SML Ltd said the company has 30-40 per cent market share in India's roughly 150,000-200,000 tonne specialty sulphur-fertilizer segment, a share it aims to lift to 50-60 per cent by 2030 through expanded field demonstrations and dealer outreach.

The company, which competes with larger rivals including Coromandel International and Deepak Fertilizers, said its patented micronized sulphur and sulphur-zinc formulations carry a higher per-unit cost than conventional sources such as gypsum and ammonium sulphate but require substantially lower application rates.

Capacity utilization at SML's production facilities stands at roughly 50-55 per cent, Shah said, with full utilization expected by 2028-29. The company plans to move some of its research capacity toward new agri-inputs beyond sulphur, including biological crop-protection products.

Founded in 1971, SML Ltd has evolved over five decades from its strong foundation in sulphur-based crop inputs into a research-driven, innovation-led global agri-solutions enterprise.
